sentences.en: When we look at the world around us, our minds are trained to fill in visual gaps to form a more complete mental picture.
sentences.zh: 当我们观察周围的世界时，大脑会习惯性地填补视觉空白，从而形成更完整的心理图像。

sentences.en: So if you see a peak of a mountain in the distance, chances are pretty good there's like a whole mountain below it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在远处看到一座山峰，很有可能下面还有整座山。

sentences.en: Yeah, and for the most part, that kind of mental extrapolation is really useful.
sentences.zh: 没错，而且在大多数情况下，这种心理推断非常有用。

sentences.en: When we notice part of a thing out in the world, our brains automatically help us see the bigger picture.
sentences.zh: 当我们注意到世界上的某一部分时，大脑会自动帮助我们看到全貌。
那是《99%隐形》的库尔特·科尔斯特德。

sentences.en: And so before we launch the bigger episode for today, Kurt and I recently encountered a small story that dovetails with something that we've covered before.
sentences.zh: 在开始今天的主题节目之前，库尔特和我最近偶然发现了一个小故事，它与我们之前讨论过的内容不谋而合。

sentences.en: It's about how our imaginations, while trying to fill in those gaps, sometimes lead us astray.
sentences.zh: 它是关于我们的想象力在试图填补这些空白时，有时是如何把我们引入歧途的。

sentences.en: And, you know, even with things that we think we visualize really well, like, for example, icebergs.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，即使是我们认为自己非常了解的事物，比如冰山。

sentences.en: Anywhere you look from like an inspirational poster to a kid's illustration, we think we know what icebergs look like.
sentences.zh: 无论你从哪里看，从励志海报到儿童插画，我们都自以为知道冰山长什么样。

sentences.en: They, you know, look like this little rounded hump on top and this sort of spike going into the water below, sort of like a big ice cream cone.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们看起来就像顶部有一个小圆包，下面伸进水里一根尖刺，有点像个大冰淇淋蛋筒。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the whole expression, tip of the iceberg.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是“冰山一角”这个成语的由来。

sentences.en: You see that little mound and you see that deep spike.
sentences.zh: 你看到那个小土堆，也看到了下面那根深深的尖刺。

sentences.en: And that's the whole point of the visual metaphor and the metaphor metaphor.
sentences.zh: 这就是视觉隐喻和隐喻本身的意义所在。

sentences.en: And I've thought about that before and I've used it a lot myself, but I never really considered it literally, like,
sentences.zh: 我以前也想过这个问题，自己也经常用这个比喻，但我从未真正从字面上考虑过它，比如，

sentences.en: as in just seeing the tips of icebergs and what that really means until I saw this image posted online by a glaciologiSt.
sentences.zh: 直到我看到一位冰川学家在网上发布的这张图片，才真正理解只看到冰山一角意味着什么。

sentences.en: So, this is an iceberg, I'm assuming.
sentences.zh: 所以，我假设这是一座冰山。

sentences.en: It's kind of a watercolor drawing.
But it's basically just like a lump of ice.
sentences.zh: 但它基本上就像一团冰。

sentences.en: It's a bit smoother than, you know, the icebergs that we are picturing in our heads before.
sentences.zh: 它比我们脑海中想象的冰山要平滑一些。

sentences.en: It's more like a stone in a river.
sentences.zh: 它更像河里的一块石头。

sentences.en: And like we've been told about icebergs in school, most of it sits below the surface of the water.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在学校里被告知的那样，冰山的大部分位于水面以下。

sentences.en: But it really doesn't look like that big cone with that deep vertical root.
sentences.zh: 但它看起来真的不像那个带有深垂直根部的圆锥体。

sentences.en: It really is like a scoop of ice cream rather than a cone.
sentences.zh: 它确实更像一勺冰淇淋，而不是蛋筒。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, part of that is what you'd expect, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，其中一部分是你所预料到的，对吧？

sentences.en: You expect only a small part of it to show up above the water.
sentences.zh: 你预料到只有一小部分会露出水面。

sentences.en: But the rest of it, what you see below, it's nothing like that cone shape, right?
sentences.zh: 但剩下的部分，你在水下看到的那部分，根本不是那种圆锥形状，对吧？

sentences.en: And the woman who drew it, her name is Megan Thompson Munson, and she's a glaciologiSt.
sentences.zh: 画这幅画的女士名叫梅根·汤普森·芒森，她是一位冰川学家。

sentences.en: And she posted this watercolor online with a really specific call to action.
sentences.zh: 她在网上发布了这幅水彩画，并提出了一个非常具体的行动呼吁。

sentences.en: Basically, she argues that we need to rethink how we represent icebergs.
sentences.zh: 基本上，她认为我们需要重新思考如何表现冰山。

sentences.en: I mean, I think I can see the problem just in her drawing itself.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我觉得光看她的画本身就能看出问题所在。

sentences.en: We're taught that 10% is above the water.
sentences.zh: 我们被教导说10%在水面上。

sentences.en: And this shows, you know, basically 10% is above the water.
sentences.zh: 而这张图显示，你知道，基本上10%在水面上。

sentences.en: But it doesn't have that deep vertical configuration.
sentences.zh: 但它没有那种深垂直的结构。

sentences.en: Because when you think about it, that doesn't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 因为当你仔细想想，那根本说不通。

sentences.en: If you put like a pool noodle in a pool, it wouldn't stand upright.
sentences.zh: 如果你把一根泳池浮棒放进泳池里，它不会直立着。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, once you think about it, you kind of get it.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，一旦你思考一下，你就会明白。

sentences.en: But you have to think about it firSt.
Urging other scientists to think about it and to draw icebergs in, quote, stable orientations.
sentences.zh: 她敦促其他科学家思考这个问题，并以所谓的“稳定方位”来绘制冰山。

sentences.en: So this is just one example, and all icebergs are presumably different.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是一个例子，所有的冰山大概都是不同的。

sentences.en: How do you know what the orientation should be?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道方位应该是怎样的？

sentences.en: Once she put this image up online, right?
sentences.zh: 一旦她把这张图发到网上，对吧？

sentences.en: This software developer came into the thread, and his name is Joshua Tauber.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫约书亚·陶伯的软件开发人员加入了讨论串。

sentences.en: And he was basically inspired by her post to make this website called Icebreaker.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是受了她的帖子启发，制作了一个名为“破冰者”（Icebreaker）的网站。

sentences.en: It just lets you draw ice shapes and see how they float.
sentences.zh: 它只是让你画出冰的形状，然后看看它们是如何漂浮的。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you draw a cone, it'll slowly reorient that cone to float on its side.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，如果你画一个圆锥体，它会慢慢调整那个圆锥体，让它侧着漂浮。

sentences.en: And you can sort of see that shift in slow motion, too.
sentences.zh: 你也可以慢动作看到这种转变。

sentences.en: So you can kind of see the physics in action.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到物理原理在起作用。

sentences.en: And in the end, it lines up in this stable orientation.
sentences.zh: 最后，它会以这种稳定的方位排列。

sentences.en: This is like you're showing me a picture of a cone.
sentences.zh: 这就像你给我看了一张圆锥体的图片。

sentences.en: And now it's definitely a cone that's, like, sadly on its side.
sentences.zh: 现在它确实变成了一个可怜地侧躺着的圆锥体。

sentences.en: So the idea with Icebreaker is you just trace out any shape, and then it'll just rotate until it finds its level.
sentences.zh: 所以“破冰者”的想法就是你画出任何形状，然后它就会旋转直到找到平衡点。

sentences.en: And that's how it would behave in nature.
sentences.zh: 这就是它在自然界中的表现方式。

sentences.en: And the site has some disclaimers, like, you know, real icebergs are three-dimensionally complex.
sentences.zh: 而且网站上有一些免责声明，比如，你知道，真实的冰山在三维上是很复杂的。

sentences.en: Their densities are going to be a little different.
sentences.zh: 它们的密度也会有所不同。

sentences.en: So the website is just sort of a simple intuition aid, more than a scientific tool.
sentences.zh: 所以这个网站与其说是一个科学工具，不如说是一个简单的直觉辅助工具。

sentences.en: And the main point is just to give you a better idea of what might happen, roughly speaking, to various shapes.
sentences.zh: 主要目的是让你更好地了解各种形状大致会发生什么。

sentences.en: And so this is, like, what if there was a cat-shaped iceberg?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是，如果有一座猫形的冰山会怎样？

sentences.en: And when you see it, it's actually a surprisingly stable configuration of the cat's head above the water and the tail above the water.
sentences.zh: 当你看到它时，猫头在水面上方和尾巴在水面上方的配置实际上出奇地稳定。

sentences.en: And, you know, odds are maybe some part of this would break off, like the tail in real life.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，很有可能现实中这部分的某些地方会断裂，比如尾巴。

sentences.en: But it does give you an idea that, like, okay, what you see above the surface and what you can imagine underwater can be very different, right?
sentences.zh: 但这确实让你明白，好吧，你在水面上看到的和你能在水下想象到的可能非常不同，对吧？

sentences.en: And it's just kind of funny.
So other than, you know, getting an accurate scientific picture to sort of combat this proverbial vision of what we have of icebergs,
sentences.zh: 所以除了为了获得准确的科学图像来对抗我们对冰山那种众所周知的刻板印象之外，

sentences.en: why is it important to visualize icebergs properly?
sentences.zh: 正确地想象冰山为什么很重要？

sentences.en: Like, why was this Megan's hill to die on?
sentences.zh: 为什么梅根要在这件事上如此坚持？

sentences.en: Well, I think it was her glacier to die on, in part because she's a glaciologiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是她必须坚持的“冰川”，部分原因是她是一位冰川学家。

sentences.en: And practically speaking, okay, there's not a whole lot of application for this, right?
sentences.zh: 从实际角度来看，好吧，这并没有太多的应用价值，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, if you're boating close to an iceberg, it is good to know that an iceberg could spread out a ways under the water.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你在冰山附近划船，知道冰山在水下可能会延伸一段距离是件好事。

sentences.en: That way, you know, you might avoid hitting it.
sentences.zh: 这样，你知道，你可能会避免撞上它。

sentences.en: But really, it speaks to this larger issue in many scientists, like geology, where so much of the world is invisible to us, right?
sentences.zh: 但实际上，它触及了许多科学领域（如地质学）中一个更大的问题，即世界上有太多东西对我们来说是不可见的，对吧？

sentences.en: So my dad, for example, is a geophysiciSt.
sentences.zh: 比如我父亲，他是一位地球物理学家。

sentences.en: And when he's explaining big planetary physical phenomena and change over time, like how tectonic plates shift around the world, visual aids are completely essential.
sentences.zh: 当他解释巨大的行星物理现象和随时间的变化时，比如构造板块如何在世界各地移动，视觉辅助工具是绝对必要的。

sentences.en: So the bigger issue is representing things more scientifically in general,
sentences.zh: 所以更大的问题是总体上更科学地表现事物，

sentences.en: whether it be icebergs in pop culture or scientific diagrams in textbooks or scientific diagrams on the news or something like that.
sentences.zh: 无论是流行文化中的冰山，还是教科书中的科学图表，或者是新闻中的科学图表等等。

sentences.en: It's like, as long as we're going to try to represent these things, we might as well get it right, you know,
sentences.zh: 就像，只要我们要尝试表现这些事物，我们最好还是把它弄对，你知道，

sentences.en: for the sake of education and for the sake of really understanding the world around us.
sentences.zh: 为了教育，也为了真正理解我们周围的世界。

sentences.en: And what this fairly specific and smaller story made me think of was Emmett's 99 PI episode on dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 这个相当具体且较小的故事让我想起了埃米特关于恐龙的《99%隐形》节目。

sentences.en: It's about how, you know, drawings have both been shaped by, but have also shaped the discipline of paleontology.
sentences.zh: 它是关于绘画如何既被古生物学塑造，又反过来塑造了这门学科。

sentences.en: And, you know, like glaciologists or geologists, paleontologists have this important role in helping us visualize things.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，就像冰川学家或地质学家一样，古生物学家在帮助我们想象事物方面也扮演着重要角色。

sentences.en: But like these other scientists, they have to extrapolate at times, too, based on whatever evidence they have.
sentences.zh: 但像这些其他科学家一样，他们有时也必须根据现有的任何证据进行推断。

sentences.en: So evidence like the fossilized bones of dinosaurs or or even the sort of modern genetic relatives of dinosaurs, that's how we extrapolate what they look like.
sentences.zh: 所以，像恐龙化石骨骼，甚至恐龙的现代基因亲属这样的证据，就是我们推断它们长相的依据。

sentences.en: And so icebergs are kind of this great contemporary physical example, but they're also this useful analogy, right?
sentences.zh: 所以冰山是一种很棒的当代物理例子，但它们也是一个有用的类比，对吧？

sentences.en: It's really easy to use icebergs to explain how we sometimes can't see what's below the surface.
sentences.zh: 用冰山来解释我们有时无法看到水面以下的东西非常容易。

sentences.en: And they hint at this larger challenge that scientists face more broadly.
sentences.zh: 它们暗示了科学家们更广泛面临的这个更大的挑战。

sentences.en: Like, how do we picture what we can't see?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们如何想象我们看不见的东西？

sentences.en: And it turns out that's a much deeper question.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这是一个更深奥的问题。

sentences.en: On that note, we're going to revisit Emmett Fitzgerald's story called Welcome to Jurassic Art.
sentences.zh: 说到这里，我们将重温埃米特·菲茨杰拉德的故事《欢迎来到侏罗纪艺术》。

sentences.en: And while listening, you might want to keep other scientific disciplines in mind because it probably applies to most of them.
sentences.zh: 在听的时候，你可能想记住其他科学学科，因为它可能适用于大多数学科。

sentences.en: Anyone who has had kids knows that they go through obsessive phases that can last anywhere from a few days to several years.
sentences.zh: 任何有孩子的人都知道，他们会经历痴迷阶段，这些阶段可能持续几天到几年不等。

sentences.en: I went through a lot of phases growing up.
sentences.zh: 我在成长过程中经历过很多阶段。
那是制片人埃米特·菲茨杰拉德。

sentences.en: There was a brief train phase.
sentences.zh: 曾有过短暂的火车阶段。

sentences.en: Then in preschool, I was obsessed with farming equipment.
sentences.zh: 然后在学龄前，我痴迷于农用设备。

sentences.en: I could list obscure European tractor brands off the top of my head like an old Italian wheat farmer.
sentences.zh: 我能像个意大利老麦农一样脱口而出列举出冷门的欧洲拖拉机品牌。

sentences.en: But I think my most intense obsession, like many kids, was dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我最强烈的痴迷，和许多孩子一样，是恐龙。

sentences.en: I knew more about dinosaurs at the age of five than I do now.
sentences.zh: 我五岁时对恐龙的了解比现在还多。

sentences.en: And I was all but certain that I would one day become a paleontologiSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我几乎确信自己有一天会成为一名古生物学家。

sentences.en: I don't know exactly where this dinosaur obsession came from, but I think part of it was just that dinosaurs looked so cool.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这种对恐龙的痴迷究竟从何而来，但我认为部分原因仅仅是恐龙看起来太酷了。

sentences.en: I had all these books filled with incredible drawings of colorful dinosaurs leaping around, roaring, and tearing into one another.
sentences.zh: 我所有的书里都画满了令人难以置信的彩色恐龙，它们跳跃、咆哮、互相撕咬。

sentences.en: I fell in love with the artwork in those books.
sentences.zh: 我爱上了那些书里的插画。

sentences.en: And at least for the time being, art is the only way we experience dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 至少目前为止，艺术是我们体验恐龙的唯一方式。

sentences.en: We can study bones and fossils, but barring the invention of time travel or some Jurassic Park resurrection scenario,
sentences.zh: 我们可以研究骨骼和化石，但除非发明了时间旅行或出现某种《侏罗纪公园》式的复活场景，

sentences.en: we will never see these animals with our own eyes.
sentences.zh: 否则我们永远无法亲眼看到这些动物。

sentences.en: There are no photos or video, which means that if we want to picture how they look, someone has to draw them.
sentences.zh: 没有照片或视频，这意味着如果我们想想象它们的样子，就必须有人把它们画出来。

sentences.en: Hello, I'm Dr. Robert Bucker, known to the folks in North Texas as Jurassic Bob.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是罗伯特·巴克博士，北德克萨斯州的人们称我为“侏罗纪鲍勃”。

sentences.en: Bob Bucker is one of the most famous living paleontologists, and he also happens to be a very skilled paleo artiSt.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·巴克是当今最著名的古生物学家之一，而且他恰好也是一位非常熟练的古生物艺术家。

sentences.en: He thinks the two go hand in hand.
Art is very important in teaching natural history science, maybe all science.
sentences.zh: 艺术在教授自然历史科学，也许是所有科学方面都非常重要。

sentences.en: Teach everyone art and everyone music, too.
sentences.zh: 教每个人艺术，也教每个人音乐。

sentences.en: When I interviewed him in a studio in Boulder, Colorado, he showed up an hour early, and he brought his own snacks.
sentences.zh: 当我在科罗拉多州博尔德市的一间工作室采访他时，他提前一小时到了，还带了自己的零食。

sentences.en: He's got coffee and some apple pie.
sentences.zh: 他带了咖啡和一些苹果派。

sentences.en: This is so liberal, this place.
sentences.zh: 这地方真是太自由派了。

sentences.en: Once we got started with our interview, Bob said that, like me, he got obsessed with dinosaurs and dinosaur art pretty early on.
sentences.zh: 采访刚开始，鲍勃就说，像我一样，他很早就对恐龙和恐龙艺术着了迷。

sentences.en: How I got hooked was a piece of journalism from 1953 Life magazine cover story called The World We Live In, and had pictures of dinosaurs and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 我入坑是因为1953年《生活》杂志的一篇封面报道，题目叫《我们生活的世界》，里面有恐龙之类的图片。

sentences.en: The cover image was the head of a long-necked dinosaur sitting in a swamp, munching on grass, with a stegosaurus in the background, sort of staring off into space.
sentences.zh: 封面图是一只长颈恐龙的头，它坐在沼泽里嚼着草，背景里还有一只剑龙，看起来像是在发呆。

sentences.en: And inside was this long article about evolution.
sentences.zh: 里面还有一篇关于进化的长文。

sentences.en: After two hours with that Life magazine, I announced to my startled parents, mom and dad, I want to grow up and be a vertebrate paleontologiSt.
sentences.zh: 看完那本《生活》杂志两小时后，我向我那吃惊的父母宣布：我长大后要当一名脊椎古生物学家。

sentences.en: And dad had no expression, and mom smiled and said, that's nice, dear.
sentences.zh: 我爸面无表情，我妈笑了笑说：真好，亲爱的。
这只是你成长过程中的一个阶段。

sentences.en: But unlike me, dinosaurs weren't just the childhood phase for Jurassic Bob.
sentences.zh: 但与我不同的是，对于“侏罗纪鲍勃”来说，恐龙不仅仅是童年的一个阶段。

sentences.en: By the time he headed off to college, a career in vertebrate paleontology was still the game plan.
sentences.zh: 到他上大学时，从事脊椎古生物学研究仍然是他的既定目标。

sentences.en: But it was kind of a strange time to be entering the field.
sentences.zh: 但那时进入这个领域有点奇怪。

sentences.en: In the mid-20th century, American dinosaur science was in a bit of a rut.
sentences.zh: 20世纪中叶，美国恐龙科学陷入了某种停滞。

sentences.en: Dinosaurs were considered big, dumb, cold-blooded reptiles.
sentences.zh: 恐龙被认为是又大、又笨、冷血的爬行动物。
注定要灭绝的进化失败者。

sentences.en: And that view of dinosaurs affected how they were painted and drawn.
sentences.zh: 这种对恐龙的看法影响了它们的绘画和描绘方式。

sentences.en: Most of the paintings of dinosaurs, they're not moving.
sentences.zh: 大多数恐龙画作中，它们都是静止的。

sentences.en: They're not interacting with each other.
There's no spark of intelligent social life.
sentences.zh: 没有一丝智能社交生活的火花。

sentences.en: And their bodies were like hulking masses of flesh.
sentences.zh: 它们的身体就像一团团笨重的肉块。

sentences.en: The way Brontosaurus and Diplodocus, the biggest dinosaurs, were illustrated,
sentences.zh: 像雷龙和梁龙这些最大的恐龙，在插画中，

sentences.en: they were like giant, gray vacuum cleaners with very, very short legs.
sentences.zh: 它们就像巨大的灰色吸尘器，腿非常非常短。

sentences.en: And they were slowly pulling themselves across the landscape or sitting neck deep in a fetid swamp.
sentences.zh: 它们要么在缓慢地拖着身体穿过地貌，要么就没入脖子深陷在恶臭的沼泽里。

sentences.en: Dinosaurs were often drawn sitting in swamps, like on that Life magazine cover.
sentences.zh: 恐龙经常被画成坐在沼泽里，就像那本《生活》杂志的封面一样。

sentences.en: The thinking was they were so large, they couldn't possibly hold up their own body weight.
sentences.zh: 当时的观点是它们太大了，根本无法支撑自己的体重。

sentences.en: And if they were drawn on land, they usually dragged their fat tails behind them as they walked.
sentences.zh: 如果它们被画在陆地上，走路时通常会拖着肥大的尾巴。

sentences.en: And that's where we were in the early 1960s.
sentences.zh: 这就是20世纪60年代初我们的认知水平。

sentences.en: Dinosaurs were sad, cold-blooded dead ends in the history of life.
sentences.zh: 恐龙是生命史上悲哀、冷血的死胡同。

sentences.en: But paleontology was about to go through...

sentences.zh: 一场壮观且意想不到的彻底转变。

sentences.en: And a young Bob Bacher, just off to college, would find himself right in the thick of the action.
sentences.zh: 而刚上大学的年轻鲍勃·巴克，发现自己正处于这场变革的中心。

sentences.en: Freshman year, the Yale Geology Department took me, a bunch of other freshmen, out to Dague.
sentences.zh: 大一那年，耶鲁大学地质系带我和其他几名新生去了达格。

sentences.en: The trip out west was led by one of Bob's professors at Yale, a paleontologist named John Ostrom.
sentences.zh: 这次西部之行由鲍勃在耶鲁的一位教授带队，他是一位名叫约翰·奥斯特罗姆的古生物学家。

sentences.en: And among other things, we dug up four raptors.
sentences.zh: 除其他发现外，我们还挖出了四只猛禽。

sentences.en: They were a new species of raptor that Professor Ostrom named Deinonychus.
sentences.zh: 它们是一种新的猛禽，奥斯特罗姆教授将其命名为恐爪龙。

sentences.en: And the bones were found really close together.
sentences.zh: 这些骨头被发现时靠得非常近。

sentences.en: But what really got Professor Ostrom excited was the anatomy of the skeleton.
sentences.zh: 但真正让奥斯特罗姆教授兴奋的是骨骼的解剖结构。

sentences.en: After studying the fossil remains back at Yale, Ostrom concluded that Deinonychus had not been a slow,
sentences.zh: 在耶鲁研究了化石遗骸后，奥斯特罗姆断定恐爪龙绝非缓慢、

sentences.en: It had been fleet-footed, agile, and extremely active.
sentences.zh: 它应该是脚步轻快、敏捷且极其活跃的。

sentences.en: Ostrom began to argue that if you really looked at the anatomy of many dinosaurs,
sentences.zh: 奥斯特罗姆开始论证，如果你仔细观察许多恐龙的解剖结构，

sentences.en: they looked less like lumbering lizards and more like super-athletic birds.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来不像笨拙的蜥蜴，而更像是运动能力超强的鸟类。

sentences.en: And his student, Bob Bakker, found this idea really compelling.
sentences.zh: 而他的学生鲍勃·巴克觉得这个想法非常有说服力。

sentences.en: He remembers looking at a skeleton of a different dinosaur called Ornitholestes.
sentences.zh: 他记得自己曾观察过一种叫鸟面龙的恐龙骨架。

sentences.en: It really did look like a roadrunner with a long, bony tail and teeth.
sentences.zh: 它看起来确实像一只长着长骨尾和牙齿的走鹃。

sentences.en: But wow, it just spoke agility.
sentences.zh: 哇，它简直就是敏捷的代名词。

sentences.en: But then you read the textbooks and you're not supposed to believe that.
sentences.zh: 但当你读教科书时，你却被告知不该相信这一点。

sentences.en: As an undergraduate, Bakker dissected modern animals in an effort to better understand dinosaur musculature.
sentences.zh: 作为本科生，巴克解剖了现代动物，试图更好地理解恐龙的肌肉结构。

sentences.en: And he concluded that the old stereotypes about stupid, sluggish dinosaurs just didn't hold up.
sentences.zh: 他得出的结论是，关于恐龙愚蠢、迟钝的旧观念根本站不住脚。
它们并不缓慢也不邋遢。

sentences.en: Now, this idea wasn't totally new.
sentences.zh: 其实，这个想法并非完全新鲜。

sentences.en: Bakker says that for decades, going back as early as the mid-19th century,
sentences.zh: 巴克说，几十年来，甚至早在19世纪中叶，

sentences.en: there had been people saying that dinosaurs were smart, active, and bird-like.
sentences.zh: 就一直有人说恐龙聪明、活跃且像鸟类。

sentences.en: But these facts were forgotten about, really.
sentences.zh: 但这些事实实际上被遗忘了。
它们从教科书中消失了。

sentences.en: So Bakker decided to publish a paper in a Yale journal.
sentences.zh: 于是巴克决定在耶鲁的一本期刊上发表一篇论文。

sentences.en: I know what you should call this study.
sentences.zh: 我知道你应该给这项研究起什么名字。

sentences.en: She said, you should call it the superiority of dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 她说，你应该叫它《恐龙的优越性》。
它们不是进化的过时产物。

sentences.en: They weren't dead ends in the flow of Darwinian process.
sentences.zh: 它们不是达尔文进化过程中的死胡同。

sentences.en: They were top of the line.
But convincing people that dinosaurs were actually totally different than they had been depicted for the past 60 years
sentences.zh: 但是，要让人相信恐龙实际上与过去60年里所描绘的完全不同，

sentences.en: was going to require more than a few good academic papers.
sentences.zh: 仅仅靠几篇优秀的学术论文是不够的。

sentences.en: To really change people's minds, sometimes you've got to show instead of tell.
sentences.zh: 要真正改变人们的想法，有时你必须展示出来，而不是仅仅诉说。

sentences.en: And remember, Bakker was a skilled illustrator as well as a scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 别忘了，巴克不仅是一位科学家，还是一位熟练的插画家。

sentences.en: And so, when John Ostrom wrote his definitive paper on Deinonychus,
sentences.zh: 所以，当约翰·奥斯特罗姆撰写关于恐爪龙的权威论文时，

sentences.en: he asked Bakker to do the illustration.
And I positioned the bones as if his raptor was running.
sentences.zh: 我把骨骼摆成了猛禽正在奔跑的样子。

sentences.en: In the picture, the raptor is nearly parallel with the ground.
sentences.zh: 在画中，猛禽几乎与地面平行。

sentences.en: Its left leg springing forward, its right leg curled tightly against its torso,
sentences.zh: 它的左腿向前跃出，右腿紧紧蜷缩在躯干旁，

sentences.en: The tail is high in the air.
It's beautiful and kind of terrifying.
Ostrom put the picture right on the front of his paper.
sentences.zh: 奥斯特罗姆把这张图放在了他论文的首页。

sentences.en: And it quickly became an iconic drawing.
sentences.zh: 它很快成为了一幅标志性的画作。

sentences.en: No one had ever seen anything quite like it.
This is Darren Naish, a paleontologist based in the UK.
sentences.zh: 这是达伦·奈什，一位常驻英国的古生物学家。

sentences.en: He's got like a flamboyant appearance.
He insists on wearing a cowboy hat all the time.
sentences.zh: 他坚持一直戴着牛仔帽。

sentences.en: He's got a giant bushy beard.
sentences.zh: 他留着巨大的浓密胡须。

sentences.en: And right from the late 60s, when he's, you know, starting to talk about this stuff,
sentences.zh: 从60年代末开始，当他开始谈论这些东西时，

sentences.en: he's drawing these agile, active dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 他画的都是这些敏捷、活跃的恐龙。

sentences.en: Bakker finished up at Yale and went off to graduate school,
sentences.zh: 巴克在耶鲁毕业后去了研究生院，

sentences.en: where he continued to speak truth to the slow, dumb dinosaur establishment.
sentences.zh: 在那里他继续向那些认为恐龙缓慢、愚蠢的权威机构说真话。

sentences.en: He wrote academic and popular articles about how impressive dinosaurs had been.
sentences.zh: 他撰写了学术和通俗文章，讲述恐龙曾经是多么令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: And he illustrated them all himself.
sentences.zh: 而且他亲自为这些文章绘制了插图。

sentences.en: He drew dinosaurs bounding across the prehistoric landscape like track and field stars,
sentences.zh: 他画的恐龙像田径明星一样在史前大地上奔跑，
有着柔韧、肌肉发达的身体。

sentences.en: So prior, prior to this time, an animal like Tyrannosaurus would have been drawn as like
sentences.zh: 所以在此之前，像霸王龙这样的动物会被画成

sentences.en: a Godzilla-type animal, dragging its tail on the ground.
sentences.zh: 哥斯拉那样的动物，拖着尾巴在地上走。

sentences.en: It's not a particularly attractive beaSt.
sentences.zh: 那可不是什么特别好看的野兽。

sentences.en: But under Bakker, you've got this thing shown with massive, bulging muscles.
sentences.zh: 但在巴克的笔下，你看到的是肌肉发达、隆起的形象。

sentences.en: And Bakker's athletic dinosaurs became a model for other paleoartists.
sentences.zh: 巴克的运动型恐龙成为了其他古生物艺术家的模范。

sentences.en: So when my Deinonychus drawing appeared, some artists younger than I said,
sentences.zh: 所以当我的恐爪龙画作出现时，一些比我年轻的艺术家说，

sentences.en: huh, okay, now we can do it.
sentences.zh: 哈，好吧，现在我们可以这么画了。

sentences.en: Artists like Gregory Paul embraced this new, exciting vision of dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 像格雷戈里·保罗这样的艺术家拥抱了这种新颖、令人兴奋的恐龙愿景。

sentences.en: They started giving their dinosaurs vibrant colors,
sentences.zh: 他们开始给恐龙涂上鲜艳的颜色，

sentences.en: and occasionally feathers to really emphasize their birdness.
sentences.zh: 有时还会加上羽毛，以真正强调它们的鸟类特征。

sentences.en: Soon, images of athletic, colorful dinosaurs were everywhere.
sentences.zh: 很快，运动型、色彩鲜艳的恐龙形象随处可见。

sentences.en: And they helped fuel the revolution that was taking place in paleontology.
sentences.zh: 它们推动了古生物学领域正在发生的革命。

sentences.en: Throughout the 70s, more and more paleontologists got on board
sentences.zh: 整个70年代，越来越多的古生物学家加入了
奥斯特罗姆和巴克的理论阵营。

sentences.en: They found new fossils and footprint evidence,
sentences.zh: 他们发现了新的化石和足迹证据，

sentences.en: suggesting that dinosaurs had been warm-blooded, intelligent, and bird-like.
sentences.zh: 表明恐龙是温血、聪明且像鸟类的。

sentences.en: This period has become known as the dinosaur renaissance,
sentences.zh: 这一时期被称为“恐龙文艺复兴”，

sentences.en: a moment when we totally rethought all of our assumptions
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，我们彻底重新思考了关于
这些不可思议的史前动物的所有假设。

sentences.en: And Darren Naish thinks art was a huge part of its success.
sentences.zh: 达伦·奈什认为艺术在这一成功中发挥了巨大作用。

sentences.en: I think that part of the reason that the dinosaurs of the dinosaur renaissance,
sentences.zh: 我认为恐龙文艺复兴时期的恐龙，

sentences.en: the dinosaurs of Ostrom and Bakker,
sentences.zh: 也就是奥斯特罗姆和巴克笔下的恐龙，

sentences.en: drew in so many scientists in the 60s and 70s,
sentences.zh: 之所以在60和70年代吸引了那么多科学家，

sentences.en: was because it was accompanied by brilliant visuals.
sentences.zh: 是因为它伴随着精彩的视觉呈现。

sentences.en: If anyone missed out on this scientific revolution
sentences.zh: 如果有人错过了这场科学革命，

sentences.en: and still thought that dinosaurs were slow and stupid,
sentences.zh: 仍然认为恐龙缓慢而愚蠢，
那这种想法在1993年终结了。

sentences.en: The dinosaurs in Jurassic Park are very active.
sentences.zh: 《侏罗纪公园》里的恐龙非常活跃。
它们就是恐龙文艺复兴的产物。

sentences.en: And when that movie came out,
the whole world got to see these fierce athletic creatures
sentences.zh: 全世界都看到了这些凶猛的运动型生物，

sentences.en: running through kitchens and eating lawyers off of toilets.
sentences.zh: 在厨房里奔跑，把律师从马桶上叼走。

sentences.en: And once you've seen the dinosaurs in Jurassic Park,
sentences.zh: 一旦你看了《侏罗纪公园》里的恐龙，
你就再也无法抹去那种印象了。

sentences.en: I think it cemented the notion of athletic dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 我认为它巩固了运动型恐龙的概念。

sentences.en: He draws dinosaurs for a living.

sentences.zh: 我是一名古生物艺术家，

sentences.en: which means that I draw and paint prehistoric animals.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我绘制史前动物。

sentences.en: Conway got interested in paleo art
sentences.zh: 康威对古生物艺术产生兴趣，
是在读了鲍勃·巴克的书《恐龙异端》之后。

sentences.en: And in the early part of his career,
sentences.zh: 他画的恐龙看起来和巴克画的很像，

sentences.en: he drew dinosaurs that looked a lot like Bakker's,

sentences.zh: 他开始觉得有点不对劲。

sentences.en: he started to feel kind of funny about it.
He says that all of his dinosaurs
sentences.zh: 看起来都像是被真空包装了一样。

sentences.en: looked like they had been shrink-wrapped.

sentences.zh: 你把衣服装进去，然后用吸尘器抽气。

sentences.en: You pack your clothes and you put the vacuum cleaner on it
sentences.zh: 你把衣服装进去，然后用吸尘器抽气。

sentences.en: and you suck all the air out
sentences.zh: 然后把里面的空气抽干

sentences.en: That's sort of what we were doing with dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 我们对待恐龙的方式也差不多。

sentences.en: We were sort of putting skin on them
sentences.zh: 我们给它们披上一层皮，

sentences.en: that was in between that skin and the muscles.
Now, paleo artists weren't just doing that
sentences.zh: 古生物艺术家们这样做，

sentences.en: to make their dinosaurs look all cool and buff.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是为了让恐龙看起来酷炫强壮。

sentences.en: They were trying to be accurate.
I am part of the generation of paleo artists
sentences.zh: 我属于那一代古生物艺术家，

sentences.en: that grew up from a young age when we first started
sentences.zh: 我们从很小的时候就开始认为，

sentences.en: to think that it really mattered to get things right.
sentences.zh: 把事情搞清楚真的很重要。

sentences.en: you want your art to be rooted in real scientific evidence.
sentences.zh: 你的艺术创作必须扎根于真实的科学证据。

sentences.en: And the main piece of evidence is often a skeleton.
sentences.zh: 而最主要的证据往往就是骨架。

sentences.en: Paleo artists would base the shape of their dinosaurs
sentences.zh: 古生物艺术家会根据准确的骨架

sentences.en: The bones give you a pretty good idea
sentences.zh: 骨骼能让你很好地判断

sentences.en: but soft tissues like skin and cartilage and fat
sentences.zh: 但皮肤、软骨和脂肪等软组织

sentences.en: Fat usually doesn't survive for millions of years in fossils.
sentences.zh: 脂肪通常无法在化石中保存数百万年。

sentences.en: And so without any evidence of it,
sentences.zh: 因此，在没有任何证据的情况下，

sentences.en: paleo artists tended to be pretty conservative
sentences.zh: 古生物艺术家在给恐龙添加脂肪时

sentences.en: about how much fat they gave their dinosaurs.
You're not going to add something
that you don't have evidence for.
sentences.zh: 你没有证据支持的东西。

sentences.en: But the result was that all these dinosaurs
sentences.zh: 但结果就是，所有这些恐龙

sentences.en: looked like they went to the gym three times a day
sentences.zh: 看起来都像是每天去三次健身房，

sentences.en: and drank protein shakes for every meal.
sentences.zh: 每顿饭都喝蛋白粉的人。

sentences.en: Well, John Conway says it began to feel
sentences.zh: 约翰·康威说，人们开始觉得

sentences.en: as though paleo artists had replaced
sentences.zh: 古生物艺术家似乎只是用一种教条

sentences.en: you know, we can't just keep doing this.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们不能一直这样下去。

sentences.en: This is not interesting in many ways.
sentences.zh: 这在很多方面都毫无趣味。

sentences.en: Is this conservative approach really giving people
sentences.zh: 这种保守的方法真的给了人们

sentences.en: the right notion about what dinosaurs looked like?
sentences.zh: 关于恐龙长相的正确概念吗？

sentences.en: Just because fat didn't survive for millions of years
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为脂肪没能保存数百万年，

sentences.en: doesn't mean that a dinosaur didn't have it.
sentences.zh: 并不代表恐龙身上就没有脂肪。

sentences.en: Animals have fat, and they have it all over the place.
sentences.zh: 动物都有脂肪，而且遍布全身。

sentences.en: And some places, they have really big fat reserve,
sentences.zh: 在某些部位，它们还有非常大的脂肪储备，

sentences.en: which changes their shape fairly drastically.
sentences.zh: 这会相当剧烈地改变它们的体型。

sentences.en: Conway asked me to consider a thought experiment.
sentences.zh: 康威让我思考一个思想实验。
如果我们像重建恐龙那样

sentences.en: if some alien paleontologist from millions of years in the future
sentences.zh: 如果未来数百万年后的外星古生物学家

sentences.en: was to try and draw a modern animal,
like, say, a whale or a camel,
sentences.zh: 画出一只现代动物，比如鲸鱼或骆驼，

sentences.en: Well, if you actually do it,

sentences.zh: 现代动物看起来会非常荒谬。

sentences.en: If you draw a bowhead whale, for example,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你只根据骨架

sentences.en: without a lot of fat or blubber,
sentences.zh: 而不加上大量的脂肪或鲸脂，

sentences.en: it looks kind of like a giant tadpole
sentences.zh: 它看起来就像一只巨大的蝌蚪，
和一条长长的、像蛇一样的尾巴。

sentences.en: I mean, you take away all that stuff
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你把那些东西都去掉，

sentences.en: and you're not left with much whale,
sentences.zh: 剩下的就不像什么鲸鱼了，

sentences.en: because whales, their shape is defined by fat.
sentences.zh: 因为鲸鱼的体型是由脂肪决定的。

sentences.en: and John argues that it would have changed their shape
sentences.zh: 约翰认为这会相当剧烈地

sentences.en: Some might have even had humps, like camels.
sentences.zh: 有些恐龙甚至可能像骆驼一样有驼峰。

sentences.en: Yeah, you could take one of the most familiar dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 没错，你可以拿一种最常见的恐龙来举例。

sentences.en: That dinosaur could have camel humps,
sentences.zh: 那只恐龙可能长着骆驼那样的驼峰，
而我们却无从知晓，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you can't tell from a camel's back
sentences.zh: 因为你从骆驼的背部骨骼

sentences.en: Now, scientists do sometimes find dinosaur fossils
sentences.zh: 科学家有时确实能发现
软组织保存完好的恐龙化石，

sentences.en: they can completely change our image of the animal.
sentences.zh: 这些化石能彻底改变我们对这种动物的印象。

sentences.en: used to be depicted in a standard shrink-wrapped kind of way
sentences.zh: 过去一直以那种标准的“真空包装”方式被描绘，

sentences.en: until paleontologists found this amazing full-body fossil
sentences.zh: 直到古生物学家发现了这具惊人的全身化石，

sentences.en: where lots of the fat and the skin
sentences.zh: 上面保存了大量的脂肪、皮肤
以及各种各样的软组织，

sentences.en: The fleshy outline around the body was quite extensive.
sentences.zh: 身体周围的肉质轮廓非常宽大。

sentences.en: It was quite a chubby creature.
